newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money stable at 3.00/03 percent.
newsitem.headline: German call money stable at 3.00/03 percent.

text.p: German call money rates were stable at 3.00/03 percent in quiet dealings on Friday ahead of the weekend with no particular change in the market trend.
But traders said rates may start to tick higher next week due to the annual summer market squeeze on rates due to the German public holidays and higher demand for cash.
"There's no general change in the market at the moment but rates may move higher next week as the holiday season gets started," said one Frankfurt dealer.
The market will also remain firm on some speculation the Bundesbank may raise rates to curb the mark's weakness.
But many traders put little confidence in the German central bank taking action anytime soon on the repo rate, which has been fixed at 3.00 percent since last summer.

Commercial bank reserves at the Bundesbank fell to 40.7 billion marks as of Thursday from 41.3 billion marks on Wednesday. The monthly average fell to 41.2 billion marks from 41.5 billion marks, which also underpinned rates.
